questions.prompt:

• The filament reaches a constant final temperature

provenance.licenseStatus: Official public contest material; personal study library

parts.label: a
parts.promptFragment:
When current flows through a filament lamp (bulb) the filament heats up.
Explain why:
• When the bulb is turned on and current flows, the temperature of the filament increases from its initial value to some higher temperature
• The filament reaches a constant final temperature
markSchemePoints: Current flows through the filament and there is a potential difference across the filament because it has electrical resistance
The electrical current transfers energy (E) to the filament (given by E = VQ or E = VIt)
Or electrical power is given by P = I²R, power is the energy transferred per unit time
The filament does not change state, the temperature increases (ΔE = mcΔθ) (owtte)
All objects (above absolute zero) absorb and radiate energy to the surrounding
The rate at which an object radiates energy to the surroundings increases as the temperature of the object increases
As the filament gets hotter, energy is radiated to the surrounds as a greater rate
At a certain temperature, the rate at which energy is radiated to the surroundings is equal to the rate at which energy is transferred to the filament by the electrical current.
At this temperature the nett change of internal energy of the filament is zero and therefore the change of temperature is also zero – the temperature remains constant

parts.label: a
parts.promptFragment:
9. A Raft

You've just learned that the buoyancy force ('upthrust') on a submerged body is equal to the weight of the water displaced by that body, and want to have some fun with it.

You decide to make a square floating raft out of 500 ml water bottles, attached together in a single layer, as shown in Fig. 11.

Your raft should be able to keep a 100 kg person completely out of the water.

Figure 11

By modelling each bottle as a cuboid with equal side dimensions, estimate the length of each side of such a raft. Explain your method. Including a simple diagram might help.
markSchemePoints: 100 kg → 100 ℓ → 200 bottles
one side = √200 bottles = 10√2 bottles
side of bottle = ∛500 cm ≈ 8 cm
or total area = 200 × (0.08)² = 1.3 m² → side ≈ 1.1 m, plus 1 mark for clarity
parts.answerText:
100 kg → 100 ℓ of water → 200 bottles
So one side is √200 bottles = 10√2 bottles

One 500 ml (cm³) cuboid bottle has a side ∛500 cm = 10 × 2^(−1/3) ≈ 8 cm
So length of a side is
10√2 × ∛500 = 10 × 2^(1/2) × 10 × 2^(−1/3) = 100 × 2^(1/6) cm = 2^(1/6) m = 1.12 = 1.1 m

Or just total area = 200 × (0.08)² = 1.3 m² giving a length of one side as 1.1 m
One mark for clarity – it is clear to you or not.
